lesson (writing): Credit each outlet only for what its own page reports: the outlets that carried Russia's defence ministry claim did not
notes: Name the vessel in the headline, lede, key points and tweet as the Panama-flagged bulk carrier Ocean Molica, also known as the Arika Sun, which CENTCOM names for this incident in the statement carried by Reuters, Dawn and The Statesman. CENTCOM says a US fighter jet struck its stern with a precision munition, disabling its propulsion without harming the crew, after it had left an Iranian port. UKMTO advisory 163-26 reports the same tanker and military forces incident in the Gulf of Oman and names no vessel, so the name is CENTCOM's, not UKMTO's.

The Black Sea item is Russia's defence ministry claim of 10 October that it struck a general cargo ship in the north-western Black Sea carrying military goods toward Odesa, with a second vessel claimed hit in Ilyichevsk port, carried by RIA Novosti, TASS and CGTN. No ship was named and there is no independent confirmation, so credit it to Russia's defence ministry and write it as a claim, never as a fact.

Write the correction in plain words for readers, with ships and dates and no internal numbering: our 8 October brief reported a Houthi claim about a Saudi oil tanker off Yanbu, and the check found the claim belongs to the 5 August 2026 attack on the Wafa, so no such attack happened off Yanbu on 6 October.
